answer.rationale: C4 shows the incumbent can be moved on both price and payment terms when benchmarked, which directly supports an 18% spend reduction without switching vendors. C6 confirms multi-year commitments with the incumbent unlock volume pricing without narrowing service scope, which strengthens the negotiating position. Together, they justify renegotiating the expiring contract with the incumbent rather than switching (c2 risk: migration + integration disruption to a line running at 94% with no buffer) or deferring (c5: month-to-month preserves flexibility but doesn't capture the cost reduction finance needs). Renewing as-is misses the 18% mandate; adding a second source (c3) is valuable for resilience but doesn't itself drive the required 18% cost cut and consumes the single decision slot.
